cases.title: Attributing 'chowkidar chor hai' findings to the Supreme Court
cases.speaker: Rahul Gandhi
cases.original_language: Hindi/English mixed; exact uninterrupted verbatim transcript pending
cases.medium: remarks to media after Rafale admissibility order
cases.claim_text: Court-recorded description: Rahul Gandhi attributed to the Supreme Court the view that 'Chowkidar (Mr. Narendra Modi, Prime Minister) is a thief'. This is not labeled a verbatim recording transcript.
testable_propositions: The Supreme Court judicially found or endorsed the assertion that Narendra Modi was a thief or guilty of Rafale corruption.
cases.confidence: high on the narrow proposition; original full recording remains to be authenticated
evidence_for: Contemporaneous recorded-video page establishes an attribution was publicly reported; judgment itself describes the attribution.
The 10 April ruling really did dismiss the Union's document-admissibility objection, as confirmed by the judgment text and contemporaneous Ministry of Defence PIB statement.
evidence_against: 15 Apr 2019 Supreme Court order explicitly disclaimed any such finding, limiting the 10 Apr decision to admissibility of documents.
14 Nov 2019 judgment paras 26-33 records attribution, unconditional apology on 8 May, and closure with caution.
Authenticated SC original 15 Apr 2019 PDF expressly rules out the alleged judicial finding; independently archived Nov 2019 judgment PDF paras 26-33 inspected.
Newly inspected 10 April 2019 Supreme Court judgment reproduction, majority paragraph 12 (printed p.18), directly limits the ruling to documentary admissibility and future review on merits.

Supreme Court's own 10 Apr 2019 judgment now directly retrieved from api.sci.gov.in: operative majority para 12 on PDF page 18 explicitly leaves review merits for later adjudication; it supplies no judicial finding of theft.
cases.counterargument: Gandhi described his rhetoric as heat-of-campaign and said the attribution was unintentional. That speaks to intent, not truth of the attributed judicial finding.
limitations: 15 Apr order and 10 Apr substantive admissibility judgment both retrieved from official Supreme Court host; judiciary-hosted 14 Nov judgment remains inaccessible, but its third-party PDF reproduction has been inspected
Whole April 10 recording and surrounding remarks not transcribed
No broader verdict here on merits of the Rafale corruption allegations
Contemporaneous video URL identified with secondary timestamp 03:05–03:18 but playback and full context not validated
New 10 Apr 2019 Economic Times publisher recording URL identified; full original video still not played or transcribed
cases.next_action: Authenticate full unedited 10 April 2019 Rahul Gandhi remarks and Hindi/English timecoded transcript; retrieve court-domain 14 Nov 2019 final judgment directly; seek human editorial review. Keep publication status draft.

cases.title: Mahadevapura: 1,00,250 allegedly stolen votes
cases.speaker: Rahul Gandhi
cases.original_language: English, based on Congress summary; full unedited video verification pending
cases.medium: press conference, Indira Bhawan, New Delhi
cases.claim_text: Congress-edited highlights: 'approximately 1,00,250 votes were stolen out of 6.5 lakh total votes in Mahadevapura.'
cases.claim_type: quantitative electoral fraud and causal allegation
testable_propositions: Exactly or approximately 100,250 fraudulent ballots were cast or counted in 2024.
Five categories of suspicious electoral roll entries reliably identify unique ineligible voters rather than overlapping entries or stale address records.
The suspicious entries caused the result in Bangalore Central to change.
BJP and ECI intentionally colluded in this alleged manipulation.
cases.confidence: moderate on failure to establish ballot theft, not a finding that rolls were clean
evidence_for: Independent field checks found mass registrations tied to changing-tenancy addresses; irregular/stale entries have support.
Five category totals supplied by Congress sum to 100,250, but arithmetic is not independent verification.
2024 ECI source records 659826 registered Mahadevapura electors, compatible with 6.5 lakh as roll denominator, but not 6.5 lakh ballots cast.
Rahul Gandhi's first-party public channel links the contemporaneous full press conference recording, creating a path to contextual claim authentication; the recording was not played.

Claimant-controlled website 31 Aug 2025 newsletter search-indexed infographic repeats the five categories and numbers. This corroborates publication of the claim, not individual electoral anomalies or illegal ballots.
evidence_against: An entry in a voter roll is not proof that a ballot was cast; no identified voter-level ballot reconciliation or deduplicated methodology retrieved.
Mobility and legitimate historic occupancy explain some high address counts, while not dispelling stale/ineligible entries.
CEO Karnataka asked for a sworn particulars-based complaint, which is an institutional response rather than proof of falsity.
ECI segment table reports only 354830 EVM votes (including NOTA) for Mahadevapura; 6.5 lakh is elector count, not EVM ballots polled.
ECI indexed constituency result reports BJP 658915 versus INC 626208, winning margin 32707; changing this margin cannot be inferred from 100250 suspicious entries without proven unique invalid votes.

10 Aug 2025 CEO Karnataka social notice, as quoted by independent contemporary reports, contests one purported instance of double voting; this is an institutional allegation pending review of its inquiry and underlying marked-roll evidence, not independently proven exculpatory evidence.

Rule 49L requires voter entry in Form 17A and a marked roll; rule 93 restricts access to the authenticated sealed records. Neither an image of two alleged ticked entries nor duplicate registrations alone proves two cast votes.

ECI August 2023 EVM manual and 15 July 2025 ECI FAQ describe Form 17C as the polling-station total vote account. Form 17A attendance differs in concept from EVM ballots polled, so any claimed double-voting count must be independently reconciled.

An August 2025 video statement attributed to the voter denies double voting, as reported by India Today. Source video and original Form 17A/marked electoral roll not inspected; testimony should be weighed, not treated as an official final adjudication.
limitations: Constituency 2024 source voter roll and supplemental logs not retrieved
Potential category overlaps not evaluated
Full 7 August 2025 claimant-owned press conference URL recovered and linked from first-party channel, but full audio/video and claim timestamps not checked

CEO Karnataka 10 August signed notice was posted on official X (URL located); attached signed original not directly inspected because X returned 403; 7 August earlier sworn-declaration letter still missing
ECI aggregate EVM votes now found; ballot-level/poll-station Form 17C, marked-roll records and eligibility adjudications not obtained

2025 Ministry of Law consolidated statute and 2023 ECI manual inspected to establish lawful route to evidence; Rule 93 sealed records need court-authorised access, and Rule 94 retention/disposal status for 2024 election packets must be confirmed rather than assuming archived copies still exist.
Direct first-person video denial reported 13 Aug 2025; raw footage provenance not verified, no protected voting register compared.
CEO Karnataka's 7 Aug 2025 X post with a letter image is now identified by exact original post ID, but the signed notice cannot be read owing to X 403. News accounts remain secondary.

Claimant-hosted 31 Aug 2025 newsletter PDF indexed text includes five category numbers, but full newsletter PDF not visually retrieved; do not treat this editorial recap as verbatim 7 Aug press conference.
cases.next_action: Authenticate full video/timecodes, signed CEO 7/10 Aug letters and inquiry annexures; seek lawful original 2024 marked-roll/Form 17A records and station Form 17C with retention check; independent category overlap audit; human editorial review.

cases.title: Ladakh: claim PM surrendered Indian territory to China
cases.speaker: Rahul Gandhi
cases.original_language: English (contemporaneous embedded post reproduction; direct original X post inaccessible)
cases.claim_text: Attributed 20 June tweet: 'PM has surrendered Indian territory to Chinese aggression.' Accompanying questions ask why and where Indian soldiers were killed.
cases.claim_type: causal attribution of territorial concession; rhetorical questions about contested border
testable_propositions: Violent 15 June 2020 Galwan confrontation and deaths occurred.
Chinese military activity disrupted patrols or attempted to alter the LAC in eastern Ladakh.
By 20 June 2020, Prime Minister personally yielded Indian sovereign territory through a decision or concession.
cases.confidence: moderate-low on causal surrender claim; substantive border incursions supported but original post and ground-control baselines pending
evidence_for: 20 June 2020 publisher embed reproduces dated claimant allegation and the prime minister's contested 19 June shorthand.
Reuters 19 June contemporaneous satellite-imagery reporting indicates significant Chinese ground activity; does not establish voluntary cession.

Defence Minister 15 September parliamentary account later acknowledges Chinese LAC transgression attempts and interference with traditional patrols; this later statement was unavailable to claimant at posting.
evidence_against: PMO 20 June clarification attributes absence of Chinese presence at the specific Galwan point to Indian armed forces' resistance; this is an interested government explanation, not independent proof.
No authenticated government cession decision, geospatial possession baseline or primary army logs were retrieved to demonstrate PM voluntarily surrendered territory.
An undemarcated and disputed LAC, temporary incursion, patrol disruption and sovereign territory transfer are distinct propositions.
cases.counterargument: The PMO's earlier categorical 19 June phrasing invited challenge and Reuters satellite findings support Chinese activity. Official rebuttals are not independent proof that all ground positions were unchanged.
limitations: Exact original X post and attached media found but inaccessible (403); contemporary media embed is a reproduction.
No raw geospatial image comparison or verifiable ground access patrol records inspected.
No primary evidence identifying a voluntary PM-directed cession by 20 June 2020; absence does not prove allegation false.
Sep 2020 official parliamentary statement and Feb 2025 MEA later answer cannot be backdated into June contemporaneous evidence.
2025 MEA question only indexed, direct original page inaccessible.
cases.next_action: Retrieve/compare original claimant post media, dated imagery and physical LAC coordinates; independent patrol records and 2020 negotiation terms; only then conduct human editorial review.

cases.title: MSP existed, but a universal statutory legal guarantee was still disputed
cases.speaker: Rahul Gandhi
cases.original_language: English passage embedded in official bilingual Lok Sabha Original Version; preceding exchange Hindi
cases.medium: Lok Sabha debate, Motion of Thanks on President's Address
cases.claim_text: “MSP is being given but kisans want MSP with legal guarantee” (official Lok Sabha original-version debate p.148; continuation criticizes government's readiness).
cases.claim_type: factual agricultural policy and statutory entitlement distinction; accompanying policy opinion
testable_propositions: Government announced/procured crops at MSP before 1 July 2024.
Existing MSP price announcements and conditional procurement were not equivalent to an across-the-board statutory legal MSP entitlement for all eligible farmers.
cases.topic: Agriculture, minimum support prices, statutory guarantee
cases.confidence: moderate-high for narrow price-policy vs general enforceable-right distinction; legal cross-jurisdiction audit still pending
evidence_for: Official 1 Jul 2024 parliamentary record p148 directly quotes Gandhi acknowledging MSP was given and explicitly distinguishing it from a legal guarantee; the MSP passage itself is not expunged.
Preclaim 19 Jun 2024 Union Cabinet decision sets Kharif 2024-25 MSP prices and lists procurement.
Preclaim Feb 2023 government reply distinguishes administrative/conditional MSP support from a general legal entitlement.
Later Jul 26 2024 official written answer treats the legal-guarantee demand as a separate question and refers to an MSP policy committee; PTI corroborates ongoing dispute.
evidence_against: Government legitimately noted existing MSP procurement, refuting a different claim that there was no MSP at all; Gandhi expressly clarified he did not claim that.
Sugarcane FRP and commodity-specific law can create narrower pricing obligations; a blanket claim that India had no legally regulated farm prices would be overbroad.
The government’s 26 July reply postdates the statement and does not prove future policy choices, and a complete central/state statute audit is outstanding.
cases.counterargument: Setting and procuring commodities at MSP constitutes substantive government support. The MP's factual point survives only when read as a demand for a generally enforceable legal guarantee, not an absence of price support. Political intent and future legislation are not judicially testable from a committee response.
limitations: Full parliamentary audiovisual playback not independently reviewed; exact English clarification in authenticated official unexpunged parliamentary transcript on printed p148.
No exhaustive central/state statute, commodity-control-order and Gazette audit completed; legal guarantee must be defined consistently.
Independent source PTI postdates claim and provides context rather than independent legal adjudication.
Do not apply result to the separate religion/violence exchange LEAD-2024-01, with expunged words and still unplayed video.
cases.next_action: Review full Sansad TV video and conduct India Code/Gazette/state law audit before genuine human editor approval. Keep public cases.json empty.
